title: Genesis 1: The Beginnings
subtitle: God creates the heavens, earth, light, and humanity in His image.
summaryHook: God creates the heavens, earth, light, and humanity in His image.
bigPictureText: Genesis opens with a majestic poem of creation: God speaks order, light, and abundant life out of empty darkness, crowning creation with humanity made in His image.
openingText: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

title: Genesis 2: Eden & Humanity
subtitle: God plants a garden paradise and forms the first human partnership.
summaryHook: God plants a garden paradise and forms the first human partnership.
bigPictureText: Zooming into Day 6, God breathes life into Adam, plants the Garden of Eden, establishes Sabbath rest, and fashions Eve so humanity is never alone.
openingText: The heavens, the earth, and all their vast array were finished.

title: Genesis 3: The Fall & Promise
subtitle: Distrust enters Eden, yet God clothes Adam and Eve with mercy and hope.
summaryHook: Distrust enters Eden, yet God clothes Adam and Eve with mercy and hope.
bigPictureText: Tempted by the serpent, Adam and Eve grasp autonomy and experience shame and exile. Even in judgment, God speaks the first promise of a future rescuer (Gen 3:15).
openingText: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”

title: Genesis 4: Cain, Abel & Mercy
subtitle: Jealousy leads to the first murder, while worship and grace continue.
summaryHook: Jealousy leads to the first murder, while worship and grace continue.
bigPictureText: Sin spreads rapidly into the first family as Cain murders Abel. Yet God protects Cain from vengeance and raises up Seth, through whom people begin calling on God.
openingText: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with Yahweh’s help.”

title: Genesis 5: Generations of Adam
subtitle: Ten generations from Adam to Noah show both mortality and faithful walking with God.
summaryHook: Ten generations from Adam to Noah show both mortality and faithful walking with God.
bigPictureText: This genealogy traces God’s image passed from Adam to Noah, pausing at Enoch—who walked so closely with God that he never saw death.
openingText: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, he made him in God’s likeness.

title: Genesis 6: Noah & the Ark
subtitle: Corrupted violence fills the earth, yet Noah finds favor and builds an ark.
summaryHook: Corrupted violence fills the earth, yet Noah finds favor and builds an ark.
bigPictureText: Grieved by human violence, God resolves to cleanse the earth with a flood while preserving Noah’s family and creation inside a massive wooden ark.
openingText: When men began to multiply on the surface of the ground, and daughters were born to them,

title: Genesis 7: The Great Flood
subtitle: The fountains of the deep burst open while God seals Noah safely inside.
summaryHook: The fountains of the deep burst open while God seals Noah safely inside.
bigPictureText: Rain falls for forty days and waters cover the highest peaks. Inside the ark, God faithfully guards Noah, his family, and every living creature.
openingText: Yahweh said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.

title: Genesis 8: Waters Recede
subtitle: A dove returns with an olive leaf, signaling a freshly washed world.
summaryHook: A dove returns with an olive leaf, signaling a freshly washed world.
bigPictureText: God remembers Noah, sends a wind over the waters, and rests the ark on Ararat. Stepping onto dry ground, Noah builds an altar of gratitude.
openingText: God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.

title: Genesis 9: The Rainbow Covenant
subtitle: God pledges never to flood the earth again and sets the rainbow in the clouds.
summaryHook: God pledges never to flood the earth again and sets the rainbow in the clouds.
bigPictureText: God blesses Noah’s family to refill the earth, affirms the sacredness of human life, and seals an everlasting covenant with the rainbow sign.
openingText: God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.

title: Genesis 10: Table of Nations
subtitle: Seventy diverse nations branch out across the earth from Noah’s three sons.
summaryHook: Seventy diverse nations branch out across the earth from Noah’s three sons.
bigPictureText: This ancient map of peoples shows how every language, tribe, and nation shares a single family origin under God’s blessing.
openingText: Now this is the history of the generations of the sons of Noah and of Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Sons were born to them after the flood.

title: Genesis 11: Tower of Babel
subtitle: Human pride builds a monument to self-glory, leading to scattered languages.
summaryHook: Human pride builds a monument to self-glory, leading to scattered languages.
bigPictureText: Humanity tries to make a name for itself rather than filling the earth. God humbles their tower by confusing languages, setting the stage for Abraham’s call.
openingText: The whole earth was of one language and of one speech.

title: Genesis 12: Call of Abraham
subtitle: God calls Abram out of Ur to become a blessing to every family on earth.
summaryHook: God calls Abram out of Ur to become a blessing to every family on earth.
bigPictureText: A pivotal turning point: God calls 75-year-old Abram to leave homeland and security behind, promising land, descendants, and global blessing.
openingText: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.

title: Genesis 13: Abram & Lot Separate
subtitle: Generous Abram lets Lot choose first and trusts God with the Canaan hills.
summaryHook: Generous Abram lets Lot choose first and trusts God with the Canaan hills.
bigPictureText: When shepherds quarrel over pastureland, Abram refuses greed and lets Lot pick the lush Jordan valley—and God reaffirms the entire land to Abram.
openingText: Abram went up out of Egypt—he, his wife, all that he had, and Lot with him—into the South.

title: Genesis 14: Rescuing Lot & Melchizedek
subtitle: Abram rescues captured Lot and receives bread and wine from Priest-King Melchizedek.
summaryHook: Abram rescues captured Lot and receives bread and wine from Priest-King Melchizedek.
bigPictureText: Abram defeats a coalition of eastern kings to free Lot, refuses plunder, and is blessed by Melchizedek, king of Salem (Jerusalem).
openingText: In the days of Amraphel, king of Shinar; Arioch, king of Ellasar; Chedorlaomer, king of Elam; and Tidal, king of Goiim,

title: Genesis 15: Covenant of Stars
subtitle: God points Abram to the night stars and seals an unbreakable covenant.
summaryHook: God points Abram to the night stars and seals an unbreakable covenant.
bigPictureText: Wondering how a childless man can father a nation, Abram believes God’s starry promise—and God credits his faith as righteousness.
openingText: After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”

title: Genesis 16: Hagar & the God Who Sees
subtitle: Fleeing mistreatment in the desert, Hagar meets the God who hears and sees.
summaryHook: Fleeing mistreatment in the desert, Hagar meets the God who hears and sees.
bigPictureText: Impatient for a child, Abram and Sarai turn to Hagar, causing painful family strife. In the wilderness, God comforts Hagar—who calls Him "The God Who Sees Me."
openingText: Now Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him no children. She had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.

title: Genesis 17: New Names & Covenant
subtitle: Abram and Sarai become Abraham and Sarah as God promises Isaac within a year.
summaryHook: Abram and Sarai become Abraham and Sarah as God promises Isaac within a year.
bigPictureText: At age 99, God gives Abraham and Sarah new names reflecting their royal future, sealing the covenant of circumcision and promising Sarah a son.
openingText: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Yahweh appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.

title: Genesis 18: Three Visitors at Mamre
subtitle: Abraham welcomes mysterious guests who promise Sarah laughter and discuss Sodom.
summaryHook: Abraham welcomes mysterious guests who promise Sarah laughter and discuss Sodom.
bigPictureText: Over a hasty desert meal beneath the oaks of Mamre, God reaffirms Isaac’s birth and invites Abraham into bold intercession for Sodom.
openingText: Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.

title: Genesis 19: Rescue from Sodom
subtitle: Angels pull Lot’s family to safety before fire falls on Sodom and Gomorrah.
summaryHook: Angels pull Lot’s family to safety before fire falls on Sodom and Gomorrah.
bigPictureText: God’s justice confronts entrenched cruelty in Sodom while His mercy drags reluctant Lot out before dawn.
openingText: The two angels came to Sodom at evening. Lot sat in the gate of Sodom. Lot saw them, and rose up to meet them. He bowed himself with his face to the earth,

title: Genesis 20: Abraham & Abimelech
subtitle: Even after Abraham repeats an old fear-driven lie, God protects Sarah.
summaryHook: Even after Abraham repeats an old fear-driven lie, God protects Sarah.
bigPictureText: Showing unflinching honesty about biblical heroes, Abraham falters out of fear in Gerar, yet God intervenes in a dream to guard the promised family.
openingText: Abraham traveled from there toward the land of the South, and lived between Kadesh and Shur. He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.

title: Genesis 21: Birth of Isaac
subtitle: Sarah’s decades of waiting turn into joyful laughter when Isaac is born.
summaryHook: Sarah’s decades of waiting turn into joyful laughter when Isaac is born.
bigPictureText: God keeps His promise right on schedule: Sarah bears Isaac ("Laughter") in old age, while God also cares for Hagar and Ishmael in the desert.
openingText: Yahweh visited Sarah as he had said, and Yahweh did to Sarah as he had spoken.

title: Genesis 22: Test on Mount Moriah
subtitle: God provides a ram substitute on the mountain, revealing "The LORD Will Provide."
summaryHook: God provides a ram substitute on the mountain, revealing "The LORD Will Provide."
bigPictureText: In the ultimate test of faith, Abraham trusts God even with Isaac. God stops his hand and supplies a ram, foreshadowing the future sacrifice on Zion.
openingText: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

title: Genesis 23: Sarah’s Burial at Machpelah
subtitle: Abraham buys a legal burial cave in Hebron, anchoring the family in Canaan.
summaryHook: Abraham buys a legal burial cave in Hebron, anchoring the family in Canaan.
bigPictureText: Mourning his beloved Sarah, Abraham purchases the cave of Machpelah—the first permanent piece of the Promised Land owned by Israel’s family.
openingText: Sarah lived one hundred twenty-seven years. This was the length of Sarah’s life.

title: Genesis 24: A Bride for Isaac
subtitle: Guided by quiet prayer at a desert well, Abraham’s servant meets generous Rebekah.
summaryHook: Guided by quiet prayer at a desert well, Abraham’s servant meets generous Rebekah.
bigPictureText: A tender love story guided by providence: Rebekah waters ten thirsty camels and courageously journeys back to marry Isaac.
openingText: Abraham was old, and well advanced in age. Yahweh had blessed Abraham in all things.

title: Genesis 25: Jacob & Esau
subtitle: Twin brothers struggle before birth and trade a birthright over red stew.
summaryHook: Twin brothers struggle before birth and trade a birthright over red stew.
bigPictureText: Abraham dies in peace; Rebekah gives birth to twins Esau and Jacob, whose lifelong rivalry begins when Esau despises his birthright for a bowl of stew.
openingText: Abraham took another wife, and her name was Keturah.

title: Genesis 26: Isaac & the Wells
subtitle: Rather than fighting over water rights, peaceful Isaac keeps digging new wells.
summaryHook: Rather than fighting over water rights, peaceful Isaac keeps digging new wells.
bigPictureText: During famine, God renews His promise to Isaac, who chooses quiet peacemaking over quarrels until God grants him room at Beersheba.
openingText: There was a famine in the land, in addition to the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.

title: Genesis 27: The Stolen Blessing
subtitle: Deception fractures Isaac’s household and sends Jacob fleeing for his life.
summaryHook: Deception fractures Isaac’s household and sends Jacob fleeing for his life.
bigPictureText: Rebekah and Jacob scheme to trick blind Isaac out of Esau’s blessing—a painful manipulation that breaks family trust for twenty years.
openingText: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see, he called Esau his elder son, and said to him, “My son?” He said to him, “Here I am.”

title: Genesis 28: Jacob’s Ladder at Bethel
subtitle: A lonely fugitive sleeps on a stone and dreams of angels bridging heaven and earth.
summaryHook: A lonely fugitive sleeps on a stone and dreams of angels bridging heaven and earth.
bigPictureText: On the run and all alone, Jacob dreams of a stairway reaching heaven. God promises to stay with him everywhere, transforming a barren hillside into Bethel ("House of God").
openingText: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and commanded him, “You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

title: Genesis 29: Jacob, Rachel & Leah
subtitle: Jacob falls in love with Rachel and works fourteen years in Haran.
summaryHook: Jacob falls in love with Rachel and works fourteen years in Haran.
bigPictureText: The trickster gets tricked by Uncle Laban! Working seven years twice for Rachel, Jacob’s complicated household begins bearing the future twelve tribes.
openingText: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.

title: Genesis 30: Twelve Sons & Flocks
subtitle: God remembers Rachel with Joseph and prospers Jacob’s spotted flocks.
summaryHook: God remembers Rachel with Joseph and prospers Jacob’s spotted flocks.
bigPictureText: Amid painful sister rivalry between Leah and Rachel, God hears their cries, grants Joseph’s birth, and multiplies Jacob’s herds.
openingText: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I will die.”

title: Genesis 31: Leaving Haran
subtitle: After twenty hard years, God directs Jacob homeward to Canaan.
summaryHook: After twenty hard years, God directs Jacob homeward to Canaan.
bigPictureText: With Laban’s envy rising, Jacob gathers his family and departs in secret. God warns Laban in a dream, ending the tension in a peaceful boundary pact.
openingText: Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ words, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s. He has obtained all this wealth from that which was our father’s.”

title: Genesis 32: Wrestling God at Peniel
subtitle: Jacob wrestles a mysterious stranger through the night and is renamed Israel.
summaryHook: Jacob wrestles a mysterious stranger through the night and is renamed Israel.
bigPictureText: Terrified of meeting Esau at dawn, Jacob wrestles God until daybreak. Limping yet blessed, he receives the name Israel ("Wrestles with God").
openingText: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

title: Genesis 33: Reconciliation with Esau
subtitle: Instead of revenge, Esau runs to embrace and weep with his returning brother.
summaryHook: Instead of revenge, Esau runs to embrace and weep with his returning brother.
bigPictureText: After twenty years of fear, Jacob bows in humility and Esau meets him with open arms—a breathtaking picture of grace and reconciliation.
openingText: Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children between Leah, Rachel, and the two servants.

title: Genesis 34: Tragedy at Shechem
subtitle: A dark chapter of violence and vengeance in Jacob’s unsettled camp.
summaryHook: A dark chapter of violence and vengeance in Jacob’s unsettled camp.
bigPictureText: After Dinah is mistreated in Shechem, Simeon and Levi respond with brutal deceit—reminding readers of the human brokenness God still works through.
openingText: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

title: Genesis 35: Return to Bethel
subtitle: Jacob’s family puts away idols, renews worship at Bethel, and mourns Rachel.
summaryHook: Jacob’s family puts away idols, renews worship at Bethel, and mourns Rachel.
bigPictureText: Returning to the place of his ladder dream, Jacob rededicates his household to God, while Rachel passes away giving birth to Benjamin near Bethlehem.
openingText: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”

title: Genesis 36: Family Line of Esau
subtitle: Esau’s descendants settle Edom and grow into kings and chiefs.
summaryHook: Esau’s descendants settle Edom and grow into kings and chiefs.
bigPictureText: Before zooming into Joseph’s epic story, Genesis records how God also blessed Esau’s family in the hill country of Seir.
openingText: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

title: Genesis 37: Joseph’s Coat & Dreams
subtitle: Favoritism and vivid dreams spark envy as Joseph’s brothers sell him into Egypt.
summaryHook: Favoritism and vivid dreams spark envy as Joseph’s brothers sell him into Egypt.
bigPictureText: Loved most by Jacob and wearing an ornate coat, teenage Joseph shares dreams of greatness—driving his jealous brothers to throw him into a pit and sell him.
openingText: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.

title: Genesis 38: Judah & Tamar
subtitle: A raw story of hypocrisy, justice, and unexpected grace in Judah’s line.
summaryHook: A raw story of hypocrisy, justice, and unexpected grace in Judah’s line.
bigPictureText: Amidst Joseph’s journey, Judah’s moral failure is exposed by Tamar’s courage—a sobering reminder that the royal line of David and Jesus rests purely on grace.
openingText: At that time, Judah went down from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

title: Genesis 39: Integrity in Potiphar’s House
subtitle: Falsely accused and thrown into prison, Joseph stays faithful and God stays with him.
summaryHook: Falsely accused and thrown into prison, Joseph stays faithful and God stays with him.
bigPictureText: Even as a slave and prisoner, "the LORD was with Joseph." Resisting Potiphar’s wife, Joseph pays the price of integrity behind prison bars.
openingText: Joseph was brought down to Egypt. Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites that had brought him down there.

title: Genesis 40: Dreams in the Dungeon
subtitle: Joseph interprets dreams for Pharaoh’s cupbearer and baker—and waits two more years.
summaryHook: Joseph interprets dreams for Pharaoh’s cupbearer and baker—and waits two more years.
bigPictureText: Even while forgotten in prison, Joseph serves fellow inmates with God-given insight into their dreams.
openingText: After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

title: Genesis 41: From Prison to Palace
subtitle: Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s famine dreams and is elevated to govern all Egypt.
summaryHook: Joseph interprets Pharaoh’s famine dreams and is elevated to govern all Egypt.
bigPictureText: Overnight, 30-year-old Joseph goes from dungeon prisoner to second-in-command of Egypt, storing mountains of grain for a global seven-year famine.
openingText: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.

title: Genesis 42: Brothers Arrive for Grain
subtitle: Guilt awakens in the brothers’ hearts as they bow before the governor they don’t recognize.
summaryHook: Guilt awakens in the brothers’ hearts as they bow before the governor they don’t recognize.
bigPictureText: Starving in Canaan, ten brothers travel to Egypt and bow face-down before Joseph—unknowingly fulfilling his boyhood dreams.
openingText: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”

title: Genesis 43: Benjamin Travels to Egypt
subtitle: Judah pledges his own safety to bring youngest brother Benjamin before Joseph.
summaryHook: Judah pledges his own safety to bring youngest brother Benjamin before Joseph.
bigPictureText: Forced back by famine, the brothers bring Benjamin to Joseph’s feast, where Joseph slips away to weep privately at the sight of his little brother.
openingText: The famine was severe in the land.

title: Genesis 44: The Silver Cup Test
subtitle: Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin’s place, proving true repentance.
summaryHook: Judah offers himself as a slave in Benjamin’s place, proving true repentance.
bigPictureText: Testing whether his brothers have changed, Joseph hides a silver cup in Benjamin’s sack. Judah’s selfless plea reveals a completely transformed heart.
openingText: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

title: Genesis 45: "I Am Joseph!"
subtitle: Through tears of forgiveness, Joseph embraces his terrified brothers and welcomes them home.
summaryHook: Through tears of forgiveness, Joseph embraces his terrified brothers and welcomes them home.
bigPictureText: One of the most emotional scenes in literature: Joseph reveals his identity and declares God sent him ahead to preserve their family alive.
openingText: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

title: Genesis 46: Israel Moves to Egypt
subtitle: God reassures aged Jacob in a night vision as seventy family members move to Goshen.
summaryHook: God reassures aged Jacob in a night vision as seventy family members move to Goshen.
bigPictureText: Leaving Canaan behind, Jacob reunites with his long-lost son Joseph in Egypt, where Israel’s family settles in the fertile pastureland of Goshen.
openingText: Israel traveled with all that he had, and came to Beersheba, and offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

title: Genesis 47: Shepherds in Goshen
subtitle: Jacob blesses Pharaoh while Joseph wisely guides Egypt through the famine.
summaryHook: Jacob blesses Pharaoh while Joseph wisely guides Egypt through the famine.
bigPictureText: Israel’s small clan flourishes peacefully in Goshen while aged Jacob prepares his final wishes to be buried back in the Promised Land.
openingText: Then Joseph went in and told Pharaoh, and said, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have come out of the land of Canaan; and behold, they are in the land of Goshen.”

title: Genesis 48: Blessing Joseph’s Sons
subtitle: Dying Jacob crosses his hands to bless Ephraim and Manasseh with enduring faith.
summaryHook: Dying Jacob crosses his hands to bless Ephraim and Manasseh with enduring faith.
bigPictureText: Adopting Joseph’s two Egyptian-born boys into the twelve tribes, Jacob recalls God’s lifelong faithfulness as his Shepherd.
openingText: After these things, someone said to Joseph, “Behold, your father is sick.” He took with him his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

title: Genesis 49: Prophetic Blessings
subtitle: Jacob speaks poetic blessings over his twelve sons, promising a coming ruler from Judah.
summaryHook: Jacob speaks poetic blessings over his twelve sons, promising a coming ruler from Judah.
bigPictureText: Gathered around his deathbed, Jacob sketches the future destiny of all twelve tribes, pointing to a royal "Lion of Judah" to whom nations will belong.
openingText: Jacob called to his sons, and said: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come.

title: Genesis 50: Meant for Good
subtitle: Joseph comforts his brothers with Genesis’s timeless motto: "God meant it for good."
summaryHook: Joseph comforts his brothers with Genesis’s timeless motto: "God meant it for good."
bigPictureText: Burying Jacob in Hebron, Joseph reassures his anxious brothers of total forgiveness: what humans meant for evil, God wove together for good.
openingText: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.

title: Exodus 1: Slavery in Egypt
subtitle: Israel multiplies in Goshen while a fearful new Pharaoh forces them into harsh labor.
summaryHook: Israel multiplies in Goshen while a fearful new Pharaoh forces them into harsh labor.
bigPictureText: Four centuries after Joseph, a new Pharaoh forgets Egypt’s debt to Israel and enslaves them—yet the more they are oppressed, the more they grow, thanks to brave midwives Shiphrah and Puah.
openingText: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):

title: Exodus 2: Baby Moses & Midian
subtitle: A baby rescued from the Nile grows up, flees to Midian, and awaits God’s timing.
summaryHook: A baby rescued from the Nile grows up, flees to Midian, and awaits God’s timing.
bigPictureText: Hidden in a papyrus basket by his mother and sister Miriam, Moses is raised in Pharaoh’s palace before fleeing to Midian—while God hears Israel’s groaning and remembers His covenant.
openingText: A man of the house of Levi went and took a daughter of Levi as his wife.

title: Exodus 3: The Burning Bush
subtitle: God reveals His holy name "I AM WHO I AM" in an unconsumed desert fire.
summaryHook: God reveals His holy name "I AM WHO I AM" in an unconsumed desert fire.
bigPictureText: Tending sheep near Horeb, Moses turns aside to inspect a bush burning without turning to ash. God calls him to free Israel and reveals His timeless covenant name: Yahweh ("I AM").
openingText: Now Moses was keeping the flock of Jethro, his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the back of the wilderness, and came to God’s mountain, to Horeb.

title: Exodus 4: Signs & Aaron Joins
subtitle: Overcoming Moses’s fears, God gives miraculous signs and partners him with Aaron.
summaryHook: Overcoming Moses’s fears, God gives miraculous signs and partners him with Aaron.
bigPictureText: Doubting his own voice, Moses learns God empowers ordinary staffs and reluctant messengers, sending older brother Aaron to stand beside him.
openingText: Moses answered, “But, behold, they will not believe me, nor listen to my voice; for they will say, ‘Yahweh has not appeared to you.’ ”

title: Exodus 5: Bricks Without Straw
subtitle: Pharaoh hardens his heart and increases Israel’s labor when Moses asks for freedom.
summaryHook: Pharaoh hardens his heart and increases Israel’s labor when Moses asks for freedom.
bigPictureText: Standing before the world’s greatest king, Moses delivers God’s demand—only to see Pharaoh retaliate by cutting straw supplies, testing Israel’s patience.
openingText: Afterward Moses and Aaron came, and said to Pharaoh, “This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Let my people go, that they may hold a feast to me in the wilderness.’ ”

title: Exodus 6: "I Will Redeem You"
subtitle: Amid crushing discouragement, God reaffirms His seven "I Will" promises.
summaryHook: Amid crushing discouragement, God reaffirms His seven "I Will" promises.
bigPictureText: When Israel is too brokenhearted to listen, God promises Moses: "I will bring you out, I will rescue you, I will redeem you with an outstretched arm."
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Now you shall see what I will do to Pharaoh, for by a strong hand he shall let them go, and by a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.”

title: Exodus 7: Staff & Nile Turned to Blood
subtitle: The showdown begins as Egypt’s sacred Nile turns to blood.
summaryHook: The showdown begins as Egypt’s sacred Nile turns to blood.
bigPictureText: Confronting Pharaoh’s magicians and Egypt’s river gods, Moses strikes the Nile with his staff—proving Yahweh is sovereign over creation.
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Behold, I have made you as God to Pharaoh; and Aaron your brother shall be your prophet.

title: Exodus 8: Frogs, Lice & Flies
subtitle: Plagues escalate across Egypt while God spares His people in Goshen.
summaryHook: Plagues escalate across Egypt while God spares His people in Goshen.
bigPictureText: Frogs, gnats, and swarms expose the helplessness of Egypt’s idols, while God draws a clear line of protection around Goshen.
entityTitles: The Ten Plagues / Signs in Egypt
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh says, “Let my people go, that they may serve me.

title: Exodus 9: Livestock, Boils & Hail
subtitle: Fiery hail devastates Egypt’s crops while warnings spare those who trust God’s word.
summaryHook: Fiery hail devastates Egypt’s crops while warnings spare those who trust God’s word.
bigPictureText: Even before hail crashes down, God graciously warns Pharaoh’s servants to bring their livestock indoors—showing mercy even amid judgment.
entityTitles: The Ten Plagues / Signs in Egypt
openingText: Then Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, and tell him, ‘This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: “Let my people go, that they may serve me.

title: Exodus 10: Locusts & Thick Darkness
subtitle: Three days of palpable darkness swallow Egypt while light shines in Israel’s homes.
summaryHook: Three days of palpable darkness swallow Egypt while light shines in Israel’s homes.
bigPictureText: Locusts strip the remaining fields and pitch darkness blankets Pharaoh’s throne, challenging the sun-god Ra while Israel enjoys light.
entityTitles: Red Sea (Yam Suph · Sea of Reeds)
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs among them;

title: Exodus 11: The Final Warning
subtitle: Moses announces the decisive midnight judgment that will finally break Egypt’s chains.
summaryHook: Moses announces the decisive midnight judgment that will finally break Egypt’s chains.
bigPictureText: After nine warnings, God prepares the final plague that will end four centuries of slavery and send Israel out with plundered treasures.
entityTitles: The Ten Plagues / Signs in Egypt
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses, “I will bring yet one more plague on Pharaoh, and on Egypt; afterwards he will let you go. When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.

title: Exodus 12: The First Passover
subtitle: Protected beneath the blood of a spotless lamb, Israel steps out into freedom at midnight.
summaryHook: Protected beneath the blood of a spotless lamb, Israel steps out into freedom at midnight.
bigPictureText: Before deliverance strikes, families gather for a hurried meal behind lamb’s blood painted on doorframes—establishing Passover as the central rescue story of the Bible.
entityTitles: The Ten Plagues / Signs in Egypt
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

title: Exodus 16: The Provision of Manna
subtitle: The Israelites’ story of hunger, grumbling, and God’s daily bread from heaven.
summaryHook: The Israelites’ story of hunger, grumbling, and God’s daily bread from heaven.
bigPictureText: Having escaped Egypt, Israel faces a major challenge: finding food in a vast desert. Instead of letting them starve, God provides a daily, sweet, flaky bread called manna—with Sabbath rules to trust His day-by-day care.
openingText: They took their journey from Elim, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after their departing out of the land of Egypt.

title: Exodus 17: Water from the Rock
subtitle: Water gushes from a desert rock at Rephidim and Joshua leads Israel in battle.
summaryHook: Water gushes from a desert rock at Rephidim and Joshua leads Israel in battle.
bigPictureText: When thirst threatens the camp, Moses strikes the rock at Horeb and fresh water pours out; soon after, Aaron and Hur hold up Moses’s hands as Joshua defends the people.
openingText: All the congregation of the children of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sin, starting according to Yahweh’s commandment, and encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.

title: Exodus 18: Jethro’s Wise Counsel
subtitle: Moses’s father-in-law Jethro reunites the family and teaches Moses to share leadership.
summaryHook: Moses’s father-in-law Jethro reunites the family and teaches Moses to share leadership.
bigPictureText: Exhausted from judging every dispute alone, Moses listens humbly to his Midianite father-in-law Jethro and appoints wise leaders across the camp.
openingText: Now Jethro, the priest of Midian, Moses’ father-in-law, heard of all that God had done for Moses, and for Israel his people, how Yahweh had brought Israel out of Egypt.

title: Exodus 19: Arrival at Mount Sinai
subtitle: Wrapped in thunder and fire, God invites freed slaves to become His "kingdom of priests."
summaryHook: Wrapped in thunder and fire, God invites freed slaves to become His "kingdom of priests."
bigPictureText: Three months out of Egypt, Israel camps beneath rugged Mount Sinai. Before giving a single command, God reminds them: "I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself."
openingText: In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on that same day they came into the wilderness of Sinai.

title: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments
subtitle: God speaks ten foundational words of love for God and neighbor.
summaryHook: God speaks ten foundational words of love for God and neighbor.
bigPictureText: Beginning with grace ("I am Yahweh who brought you out of slavery"), the Ten Commandments establish rhythms of worship, Sabbath rest, family honor, and integrity.
openingText: God spoke all these words, saying,

title: Exodus 21: Dignity & Justice Laws
subtitle: Practical case laws protecting servants, the injured, and vulnerable workers.
summaryHook: Practical case laws protecting servants, the injured, and vulnerable workers.
bigPictureText: Moving straight from Sinai’s thunder to everyday life, these laws curb revenge ("eye for an eye" as a maximum limit) and defend human dignity.
openingText: “Now these are the ordinances which you shall set before them:

title: Exodus 22: Compassion for the Vulnerable
subtitle: God commands fierce protection for foreigners, widows, orphans, and the poor.
summaryHook: God commands fierce protection for foreigners, widows, orphans, and the poor.
bigPictureText: Remembering they were once strangers in Egypt, Israel is called to practice fairness, restitution, and generous kindness toward the vulnerable.
openingText: “If a man steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.

title: Exodus 23: Sabbath Year & Sacred Feasts
subtitle: Rhythms of rest for the land, impartial justice, and three joyful annual festivals.
summaryHook: Rhythms of rest for the land, impartial justice, and three joyful annual festivals.
bigPictureText: Even farmland gets a Sabbath rest every seventh year! God sets a calendar of celebration and promises His Angel will guide Israel home.

summaryHook: Moses and the elders dine in God’s presence beneath a sky-blue sapphire pavement.
bigPictureText: Sealing the Sinai covenant, Israel’s leaders climb partway up the mountain and share a peaceful covenant meal seeing God’s radiant glory.

title: Exodus 25: Blueprint of the Tabernacle
subtitle: God asks for willing hearts to build a portable sanctuary so He can dwell among them.
summaryHook: God asks for willing hearts to build a portable sanctuary so He can dwell among them.
bigPictureText: God’s desire isn’t to stay distant on a mountain—He gives detailed designs for the Ark, Mercy Seat, Table of Bread, and Golden Lampstand.

summaryHook: Woven linen curtains of blue, purple, and scarlet frame God’s portable home.
bigPictureText: Like a mobile Garden of Eden stitched with cherubim, the Tabernacle’s layered curtains create a breathtaking tent in the center of the camp.

summaryHook: An outer courtyard welcomes worshipers with bronze offerings and perpetual olive-oil light.
bigPictureText: Every detail—from the bronze altar to the pure olive oil lamp burning from evening till morning—invites Israel near to God.

summaryHook: Aaron wears twelve gemstones over his heart, carrying Israel’s names before God.

subtitle: Seven days of cleansing and anointing set Aaron and his sons apart to serve.
summaryHook: Seven days of cleansing and anointing set Aaron and his sons apart to serve.
bigPictureText: A solemn ceremony prepares the priests to mediate worship so God’s holiness can dwell safely right in the middle of the people.

title: Exodus 30: Incense Altar & Anointing Oil
subtitle: Fragrant morning and evening incense rises like prayer inside the sanctuary.
summaryHook: Fragrant morning and evening incense rises like prayer inside the sanctuary.
bigPictureText: Blending aromatic spices and ransom silver equal for rich and poor alike, God establishes prayerful rhythms at the heart of the camp.

subtitle: Impatient while Moses is on the mountain, the camp casts a golden idol—and Moses pleads for mercy.
summaryHook: Impatient while Moses is on the mountain, the camp casts a golden idol—and Moses pleads for mercy.
bigPictureText: Like wedding vows broken on the honeymoon, Israel worships a golden calf. Moses intercedes selflessly, begging God to blot out his own name rather than destroy the people.
openingText: When the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, the people gathered themselves together to Aaron, and said to him, “Come, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we don’t know what has become of him.”

title: Exodus 33: "Show Me Your Glory"
subtitle: In the Tent of Meeting, Moses speaks with God face to face and asks to see His glory.
summaryHook: In the Tent of Meeting, Moses speaks with God face to face and asks to see His glory.
bigPictureText: Refusing to travel one step without God’s presence, Moses pleads "Show me Your glory!"—and God hides him in the cleft of the rock.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, “Depart, go up from here, you and the people that you have brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your offspring.’

title: Exodus 34: The Compassionate Name of God
subtitle: Passing before Moses, God proclaims Himself "merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love."
summaryHook: Passing before Moses, God proclaims Himself "merciful, gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love."
bigPictureText: Exodus 34:6–7 becomes the most quoted verse in the entire Bible: when renewing the broken tablets, God defines His deepest nature as forgiving, steadfast love.

title: Exodus 35: Generous Hearts Bring Offerings
subtitle: Moved with joy, men and women bring gold, yarn, and skills—more than enough!
summaryHook: Moved with joy, men and women bring gold, yarn, and skills—more than enough!
bigPictureText: Responding to God’s grace after the golden calf, the whole community gives so generously toward the Tabernacle that Moses actually has to ask them to stop!
openingText: Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said to them, “These are the words which Yahweh has commanded, that you should do them.

subtitle: Bezalel, Oholiab, and skilled artisans weave the curtains and frames together.
summaryHook: Bezalel, Oholiab, and skilled artisans weave the curtains and frames together.
bigPictureText: Craftspeople turn generous gifts into sacred architecture, assembling the acacia wood frames and embroidered curtains step by step.
openingText: “Bezalel and Oholiab shall work with every wise-hearted man, in whom Yahweh has put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that Yahweh has commanded.”

summaryHook: Golden cherubim stretch wings over the Mercy Seat while the seven-branched menorah shines.

openingText: Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood. Its length was two and a half cubits, and its width a cubit and a half, and a cubit and a half its height.

summaryHook: Bronze mirrors donated by women become the washing basin as every material is accounted for.
bigPictureText: Even the bronze mirrors of worshiping women are repurposed into the sanctuary laver, alongside an honest public audit of every ounce of gold and silver.

summaryHook: Every garment and gemstone is finished "just as Yahweh commanded Moses," and Moses blesses them.
bigPictureText: Inspecting the finished sanctuary and priestly robes, Moses sees total obedience and blesses the workers—echoing God’s blessing over finished Creation.
openingText: Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

title: Exodus 40: Glory Fills the Tabernacle

summaryHook: Moses erects the Tabernacle, and God’s radiant cloud fills the house for the journey ahead.
bigPictureText: Exodus ends in awe: the God who created the cosmos and rescued slaves from Egypt now moves right into a tent in the middle of His people’s camp.

title: Leviticus 1: The Burnt Offering
subtitle: God calls from the Tent of Meeting, inviting worshipers to "draw near" with wholehearted devotion.
summaryHook: God calls from the Tent of Meeting, inviting worshipers to "draw near" with wholehearted devotion.
bigPictureText: Starting directly from Exodus 40 where God moved into the Tabernacle, Leviticus opens with "korban" (drawing near): a voluntary burnt offering symbolizing total surrender and forgiveness.
openingText: Yahweh called to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,

title: Leviticus 2: The Grain Offering
subtitle: Bringing daily flour, olive oil, and frankincense in gratitude—with zero leaven and covenant salt.
summaryHook: Bringing daily flour, olive oil, and frankincense in gratitude—with zero leaven and covenant salt.
bigPictureText: A bloodless offering of everyday baked bread and roasted grain! Worshipers bring the fruit of their daily labor to thank God for daily bread.
openingText: “ ‘When anyone offers an offering of a meal offering to Yahweh, his offering shall be of fine flour. He shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.

title: Leviticus 3: The Peace Offering
subtitle: A joyful fellowship meal shared between God, the priests, and the worshiper’s family.
summaryHook: A joyful fellowship meal shared between God, the priests, and the worshiper’s family.
bigPictureText: More than an apology for sin, the Peace Offering ("Shalom" offering) was a celebratory barbecue in God’s courtyard celebrating friendship and wholeness with God.
openingText: “ ‘If his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before Yahweh.

title: Leviticus 4: The Sin Offering
subtitle: Cleaning up unintentional mistakes—scaled gracefully from leaders down to the poorest.
summaryHook: Cleaning up unintentional mistakes—scaled gracefully from leaders down to the poorest.
bigPictureText: Honoring the truth that everyone stumbles unintentionally, God provides atonement scaled by income—even allowing a handful of flour for those who cannot afford a lamb (Ch 5).
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 5: Guilt & Restitution
subtitle: Making things right with God and paying back harmed neighbors plus twenty percent.
summaryHook: Making things right with God and paying back harmed neighbors plus twenty percent.
bigPictureText: True repentance isn’t vague—it repairs broken trust with people. When someone wronged a neighbor, they returned what was stolen plus extra restitution before bringing their offering.
openingText: “ ‘If anyone sins, in that he hears a public adjuration to testify, he being a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he doesn’t report it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

title: Leviticus 6: The Fire Never Goes Out
subtitle: Priests keep the altar fire burning continuously—day and night—as a sign of unceasing grace.
summaryHook: Priests keep the altar fire burning continuously—day and night—as a sign of unceasing grace.
bigPictureText: Shifting to the priests’ perspective, God commands that the altar flame must never die out, assuring Israel that God’s welcome stays open around the clock.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 7: Sharing the Feast of Peace
subtitle: Instructions for eating thanksgiving offerings promptly with friends and neighbors.
summaryHook: Instructions for eating thanksgiving offerings promptly with friends and neighbors.
bigPictureText: Peace offerings had to be eaten quickly while fresh—encouraging worshipers to invite family, friends, and the needy to share the feast together.
openingText: “ ‘This is the law of the trespass offering: It is most holy.

subtitle: Washing, robing, and anointing the priests for seven days at the entrance of the Tent.
summaryHook: Washing, robing, and anointing the priests for seven days at the entrance of the Tent.
bigPictureText: In front of the whole congregation, Moses washes and clothes Aaron and his four sons, consecrating their ears, thumbs, and toes to listen, act, and walk faithfully.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

summaryHook: Aaron blesses the people and heavenly fire lights the altar while the camp falls down in joyful awe.
bigPictureText: On the eighth day, Moses and Aaron bless Israel together, and fire flashes out from Yahweh’s presence to accept the offerings—sparking a joyful shout from the whole nation.
openingText: On the eighth day, Moses called Aaron and his sons, and the elders of Israel;

subtitle: Nadab and Abihu’s rash "unauthorized fire" teaches the weighty beauty of honoring God’s holiness.
summaryHook: Nadab and Abihu’s rash "unauthorized fire" teaches the weighty beauty of honoring God’s holiness.
bigPictureText: A sobering reminder that drawing near to a holy God calls for reverence rather than carelessness—followed by Aaron’s silent grief and Eleazar & Ithamar stepping forward.
openingText: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, each took his censer, and put fire in it, and laid incense on it, and offered strange fire before Yahweh, which he had not commanded them.

subtitle: Daily dietary reminders distinguishing Israel as God’s set-apart people at every mealtime.
summaryHook: Daily dietary reminders distinguishing Israel as God’s set-apart people at every mealtime.
bigPictureText: More than ancient health guidelines, kosher food laws turned every ordinary breakfast and dinner into a quiet reminder of belonging to a holy God.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying to them,

title: Leviticus 12: New Birth & Purification
subtitle: Ceremonies honoring mothers after childbirth, scaling offerings gracefully for humble families.
summaryHook: Ceremonies honoring mothers after childbirth, scaling offerings gracefully for humble families.
bigPictureText: Marking the sacred threshold of new life, mothers brought a lamb—or two turtledoves if poor (the exact humble offering Mary and Joseph later brought for Jesus in Luke 2!).
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 13: Caring Through Quarantine
subtitle: Priests act as compassionate health inspectors to examine skin diseases and protect the community.
summaryHook: Priests act as compassionate health inspectors to examine skin diseases and protect the community.
bigPictureText: Priests didn’t shun the sick out of cruelty—they carefully diagnosed skin conditions, quarantined contagious cases to protect families, and longed to declare people healed.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

title: Leviticus 14: Restored to Community
subtitle: Birds set free over running water celebrate a healed person’s joyful return to camp.
summaryHook: Birds set free over running water celebrate a healed person’s joyful return to camp.
bigPictureText: Containing detailed restoration rituals for healed skin disease—including releasing a live bird into open fields—this chapter celebrates full return to worship and community.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 15: Sacred Life & Boundaries
subtitle: Respectful washing rituals protecting community health and highlighting the sacredness of life.
summaryHook: Respectful washing rituals protecting community health and highlighting the sacredness of life.
bigPictureText: Routine bodily discharges required simple water washing and patience until evening—reminding Israel that God’s Tabernacle was a place of wholeness and life.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

summaryHook: Yom Kippur: once a year the High Priest enters the Holy of Holies and a scapegoat carries sins away.
bigPictureText: The center and heartbeat of Leviticus! On Yom Kippur, one goat’s blood cleanses the sanctuary while the second goat ("scapegoat") carries Israel’s sins far out into the wilderness—never to return.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses after the death of the two sons of Aaron, when they came near before Yahweh, and died;

title: Leviticus 17: "The Life Is in the Blood"
subtitle: Because blood represents life itself, God guards it with reverence as the means of atonement.
summaryHook: Because blood represents life itself, God guards it with reverence as the means of atonement.
bigPictureText: Explaining why ancient sacrifices mattered, God declares "the life of the flesh is in the blood"—not as magic, but as life offered on the altar to make atonement.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 18: Healthy Family Boundaries
subtitle: Protecting marriage, children, and dignity in contrast to cruel surrounding empires.
summaryHook: Protecting marriage, children, and dignity in contrast to cruel surrounding empires.
bigPictureText: Setting Israel apart from practices like child sacrifice and family exploitation in Egypt and Canaan, God protects vulnerable relatives and the sanctity of the home.
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses,

title: Leviticus 19: "Love Your Neighbor"
subtitle: Everyday holiness means leaving harvest edges for the poor, paying fair wages, and loving neighbors.
summaryHook: Everyday holiness means leaving harvest edges for the poor, paying fair wages, and loving neighbors.
bigPictureText: One of the greatest chapters in Scripture! Holiness isn’t hiding in a monastery—it looks like refusing to gossip, welcoming immigrants, using honest scales, and "loving your neighbor as yourself" (19:18).
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 20: Be Holy Because I Am Holy
subtitle: Serious community protections against child sacrifice and destructive abuses.
summaryHook: Serious community protections against child sacrifice and destructive abuses.
bigPictureText: Repeating the call to reflect God’s character, Israel is reminded that rejecting oppressive idol customs keeps the land healthy and blessed.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 21: Integrity of Spiritual Leaders
subtitle: High standards of wholeness and compassion for priests who serve before God’s altar.
summaryHook: High standards of wholeness and compassion for priests who serve before God’s altar.
bigPictureText: Because priests represented both God to the people and the people to God, their daily conduct and reverence reflected the beauty of the sanctuary.
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses, “Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and say to them, ‘A priest shall not defile himself for the dead among his people,

title: Leviticus 22: Offering Our Very Best
subtitle: Unblemished offerings honor the greatness of the God who rescues and sanctifies.
summaryHook: Unblemished offerings honor the greatness of the God who rescues and sanctifies.
bigPictureText: Bringing leftovers or sick animals showed disrespect; bringing unblemished gifts honored the living God who had rescued Israel from Egypt.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 23: The Seven Sacred Feasts
subtitle: Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Pentecost, Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles—a calendar of joy.
summaryHook: Sabbath, Passover, Firstfruits, Pentecost, Trumpets, Atonement, and Tabernacles—a calendar of joy.
bigPictureText: God built celebration right into Israel’s calendar! Seven annual festivals retold rescue, harvest gratitude, atonement, and camping under starry booths remembering the wilderness.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 24: Perpetual Light & Justice
subtitle: Golden lampstand oil, twelve loaves of Bread of the Presence, and equal justice under the law.
summaryHook: Golden lampstand oil, twelve loaves of Bread of the Presence, and equal justice under the law.
bigPictureText: Pure olive oil keeps the seven-branched menorah shining beside twelve fresh Sabbath loaves representing all twelve tribes—paired with impartial law for citizen and foreigner alike.
openingText: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

title: Leviticus 25: The Year of Jubilee

summaryHook: Every fiftieth year, trumpets sound liberty: debts are canceled, slaves freed, and family land restored.
bigPictureText: A breathtaking economic reset! Every 7th year the soil rests, and every 50th year ("Jubilee") cancels generational poverty so every family returns home free—quoted by Jesus in Luke 4!
openingText: Yahweh said to Moses in Mount Sinai,

summaryHook: Obedience brings rain and peace; even if exile comes, God vows never to forget His covenant.
bigPictureText: Setting out the blessings of walking closely with God—peace, rain, and God walking right among them—alongside warnings and a promise that repentance always restores.
openingText: “ ‘You shall make for yourselves no idols, and you shall not raise up a carved image or a pillar, and you shall not place any figured stone in your land, to bow down to it; for I am Yahweh your God.

title: Leviticus 27: Sacred Vows & Dedication
subtitle: Devoting gifts, homes, fields, and tithes willingly to support worship and the community.
summaryHook: Devoting gifts, homes, fields, and tithes willingly to support worship and the community.
bigPictureText: Leviticus concludes on voluntary generosity: when people make special vows of gratitude, fair valuations protect families while funding the sanctuary.

bigPictureText: One month after the Tabernacle is raised, God commands a census of every tribe—organizing Israel not as a disorganized mob, but as a structured community centered on God’s dwelling.

summaryHook: Twelve tribes pitch their tents in four directions with God’s Tabernacle in the middle.

bigPictureText: Replacing the firstborn sons spared at Passover, the Levites (Kohath, Gershon, Merari) serve around Aaron’s priests to keep sacred worship orderly.
