subtitle: Covered in sores outside the gate, Job sits quietly in ashes as three friends weep for seven days.
summaryHook: Covered in sores outside the gate, Job sits quietly in ashes as three friends weep for seven days.
bigPictureText: Rejecting bitterness even when his own health collapses, Job asks simply: “Shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil?”
openingText: Again, on the day when the God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan came also among them to present himself before Yahweh.

title: Job 3: Cursing the Day of Birth
subtitle: After seven days of heavy silence, Job pours out raw lament begging simply for rest from pain.
summaryHook: After seven days of heavy silence, Job pours out raw lament begging simply for rest from pain.
bigPictureText: God preserves honest grief without sugarcoating it—showing that faith can weep aloud in darkness without losing honesty.
openingText: After this Job opened his mouth, and cursed the day of his birth.

title: Job 4: Eliphaz’s First Reply & Night Vision
subtitle: Elder Eliphaz reminds Job of how he once strengthened weak knees before questioning his suffering.
summaryHook: Elder Eliphaz reminds Job of how he once strengthened weak knees before questioning his suffering.
bigPictureText: Gentle in tone yet rigid in theology, Eliphaz assumes innocent people never perish—a tidy formula pain will soon shatter.
openingText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 5: Appeals, Discipline & Morning Rain
subtitle: Eliphaz urges Job to commit his cause to God, who heals wounds and sends rain across dusty fields.
summaryHook: Eliphaz urges Job to commit his cause to God, who heals wounds and sends rain across dusty fields.
bigPictureText: Truthful poetry about God lifting the lowly collides painfully with Eliphaz’s assumption that Job must have earned his affliction.
openingText: “Call now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the holy ones will you turn?

title: Job 6: Pain Heavier Than the Sand of Seas
subtitle: Job begs his friends to weigh his anguish honestly instead of preaching like dry desert brooks.
summaryHook: Job begs his friends to weigh his anguish honestly instead of preaching like dry desert brooks.
bigPictureText: Comparing fair-weather friends to wadis that freeze in winter and vanish in summer, Job longs simply for loyal kindness.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 7: Weary Nights & “Why Watch Me?”
subtitle: Sleepless until dawn, Job cries directly to God about how brief and fragile human breath feels.
summaryHook: Sleepless until dawn, Job cries directly to God about how brief and fragile human breath feels.
bigPictureText: Rather than hiding from God behind polite clichés, agonizing Job argues candidly with his Maker through the long dark watch.
openingText: “Isn’t a man forced to labor on earth? Aren’t his days like the days of a hired hand?

title: Job 8: Bildad & the Ancient Sages
subtitle: Bildad the Shuhite appeals to past generations, insisting God never drops the upright.
summaryHook: Bildad the Shuhite appeals to past generations, insisting God never drops the upright.
bigPictureText: Traditional proverbs ring cold and mechanical when applied like a hammer against a grieving father’s fresh wounds.
openingText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

title: Job 9: How Can Mortal Stand Before God?
subtitle: Gazing at Orion and mountains moved by God’s hand, Job longs for a mediator between sky and dust.
summaryHook: Gazing at Orion and mountains moved by God’s hand, Job longs for a mediator between sky and dust.
bigPictureText: Confessing that no mortal can out-argue the Creator of constellations, Job aches for an umpire who can lay a hand on both sides.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 10: Clay Hands & Remembered Mercy
subtitle: “You clothed me with skin and flesh, knit me together with bones and sinews.”
summaryHook: “You clothed me with skin and flesh, knit me together with bones and sinews.”
bigPictureText: Reminding God of his tender craftsmanship in forming him, Job pleads to know why his Creator now feels so distant.
openingText: “My soul is weary of my life. I will give free course to my complaint. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.

title: Job 11: Zophar’s Sharp Rebuke
subtitle: Zophar insists God’s wisdom is higher than heaven and hints Job deserves even worse.
summaryHook: Zophar insists God’s wisdom is higher than heaven and hints Job deserves even worse.
bigPictureText: Mistaking blunt certainty for spiritual insight, Zophar lectures a broken friend instead of sitting in compassionate mercy.
openingText: Then Zophar, the Naamathite, answered,

title: Job 12: Ask the Beasts & Birds of Sky
subtitle: “In his hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.”
summaryHook: “In his hand is the life of every living thing, and the breath of all mankind.”
bigPictureText: Answering with wry clarity that wisdom won’t die with his three critics, Job points straight to earth, sea, and sky.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 13: Though He Slay Me, Yet I Trust
subtitle: Job dismisses his friends as worthless physicians and insists on pleading directly before God.
summaryHook: Job dismisses his friends as worthless physicians and insists on pleading directly before God.
bigPictureText: Rising to courageous faith amid agony, Job resolves to stand before God openly—preferring honest truth to pious flattery.
openingText: “Behold, my eye has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.

title: Job 14: Hope for a Cut-Down Tree
subtitle: Watching green shoots sprout from an aged stump at the scent of water, Job wonders if life can bloom again.
summaryHook: Watching green shoots sprout from an aged stump at the scent of water, Job wonders if life can bloom again.
bigPictureText: Poetic longing watches nature revive after rain, yearning for God to hide him safely until storm clouds pass and call his name.
openingText: “Man, who is born of a woman, is of few days, and full of trouble.

title: Job 15: Eliphaz Hardens Into Warning
subtitle: Pushed by Job’s boldness, Eliphaz warns against casting off fear in the quiet assembly.
summaryHook: Pushed by Job’s boldness, Eliphaz warns against casting off fear in the quiet assembly.
bigPictureText: When neat formulas fail to comfort, well-meaning friends often turn defensive—painting grim portraits of doom.
openingText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 16: My Witness Is High in Heaven
subtitle: Calling his friends miserable comforters, Job looks above earth toward a heavenly Advocate.
summaryHook: Calling his friends miserable comforters, Job looks above earth toward a heavenly Advocate.
bigPictureText: Even while feeling pierced from every side, faith breaks through: “Even now, behold, my witness is in heaven, and he who vouches for me is on high.”
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 17: Broken Spirit & Steadfast Hands
subtitle: Surrounded by mockers as his eyes grow dim with sorrow, Job holds fast to clean hands.
summaryHook: Surrounded by mockers as his eyes grow dim with sorrow, Job holds fast to clean hands.
bigPictureText: Choosing quiet endurance even when every earthly plan lies broken, the upright keep walking forward step by step.
openingText: “My spirit is consumed. My days are extinct, and the grave is ready for me.

title: Job 18: Bildad Describes the Snare & Dark Lamp
subtitle: Stung by Job’s sharp words, Bildad recites how every wicked household’s light goes out.
summaryHook: Stung by Job’s sharp words, Bildad recites how every wicked household’s light goes out.
bigPictureText: By repeating dark warnings about extinction, Bildad shows how fearful theology can trample an innocent sufferer.
openingText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

title: Job 19: “I Know That My Redeemer Lives!”
subtitle: Carved in rock forever, Job’s sudden confession of a living Redeemer blazes above loneliness.
summaryHook: Carved in rock forever, Job’s sudden confession of a living Redeemer blazes above loneliness.
bigPictureText: Forgotten by neighbors and misunderstood by friends, Job proclaims with startling assurance that after ashes fade his eyes will see God.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 20: Zophar on Fleeting Ill-Gotten Wealth
subtitle: Hasty Zophar insists every feast of greed turns bitter before sunset.
summaryHook: Hasty Zophar insists every feast of greed turns bitter before sunset.
bigPictureText: Blind to Job’s blameless life, Zophar applies textbook retribution against a man mourning empty rooms.
openingText: Then Zophar the Naamathite answered,

title: Job 21: Why Do the Prosperous Ignore Reality?
subtitle: Job challenges his friends’ tidy rule by pointing to harsh people living comfortably till old age.
summaryHook: Job challenges his friends’ tidy rule by pointing to harsh people living comfortably till old age.
bigPictureText: Refusing polite falsehoods to defend God, Job insists real faith faces complex life honestly rather than lying for religion’s sake.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 22: Eliphaz’s Unjust Accusations
subtitle: Desperate to protect his system, Eliphaz invents imaginary sins against hungry widows and orphans.
summaryHook: Desperate to protect his system, Eliphaz invents imaginary sins against hungry widows and orphans.
bigPictureText: A sober warning: clinging too tightly to an unbending rule can tempt us to slander innocent neighbors just to stay “right.”
openingText: Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered,

title: Job 23: “Oh That I Knew Where I Might Find Him!”
subtitle: Searching forward, backward, left, and right, Job trusts God knows the way he takes.
summaryHook: Searching forward, backward, left, and right, Job trusts God knows the way he takes.
bigPictureText: Though God feels hidden beyond sight, Job clings to radiant confidence: “When he has tried me, I shall come out like gold.”
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 24: Tears of the Poor Left Unanswered
subtitle: Job lists field laborers, orphans, and night thieves waiting long for justice on earth.
summaryHook: Job lists field laborers, orphans, and night thieves waiting long for justice on earth.
bigPictureText: Crying over widespread injustice across the world, Job refuses to pretend the earth runs cleanly on quick instant rewards.
openingText: “Why aren’t times laid up by the Almighty? Why don’t those who know him see his days?

title: Job 25: Bildad’s Brief Hymn on Dominion
subtitle: Falling short of answers, Bildad ends his counsel in six short verses before cosmic Majesty.
summaryHook: Falling short of answers, Bildad ends his counsel in six short verses before cosmic Majesty.
bigPictureText: When human arguments run dry, all Bildad can murmur is that stars shine small beside the Holy One.
openingText: Then Bildad the Shuhite answered,

title: Job 26: Hanging the Earth Upon Nothing
subtitle: Job answers with sweeping awe: God stretches the north over empty space and wraps rain inside clouds.
summaryHook: Job answers with sweeping awe: God stretches the north over empty space and wraps rain inside clouds.
bigPictureText: Even these towering wonders, Job marvels, are merely the outer fringes of God’s whisper—how small our loudest wisdom sounds.
openingText: Then Job answered,

title: Job 27: Holding Fast to Integrity
subtitle: As the silence lengthens, Job vows never to pretend guilt just to please watching critics.
summaryHook: As the silence lengthens, Job vows never to pretend guilt just to please watching critics.
bigPictureText: With unshakable honesty, Job declares that as long as breath remains in his nostrils his lips will speak no deceit.
openingText: Job again took up his parable, and said,

title: Job 28: Mining Gold, Yet Where Is Wisdom?
subtitle: Humanity cuts glowing crystal tunnels deep underground—yet true wisdom cannot be bought with gold.
summaryHook: Humanity cuts glowing crystal tunnels deep underground—yet true wisdom cannot be bought with gold.
bigPictureText: A gleaming poetic interlude pauses the debate to reveal that reverence for the Lord and turning from evil are wisdom’s true treasure.
openingText: “Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for gold which they refine.

title: Job 29: Remembering Days When His Lamp Shone
subtitle: Job recalls walking through town gates respected, rescuing the poor, and lighting orphaned homes.
summaryHook: Job recalls walking through town gates respected, rescuing the poor, and lighting orphaned homes.
bigPictureText: Tender memories of fatherly justice, open doors, and evening dewdrops highlight how deeply integrity shaped Job’s quiet life.
openingText: Job again took up his parable, and said,

title: Job 30: Now Mocked in Dust & Ashes
subtitle: Painful contrast strips away honor as younger voices jeer and fever grips his nights.
summaryHook: Painful contrast strips away honor as younger voices jeer and fever grips his nights.
bigPictureText: Pouring out the sharp sting of public shame alongside physical agony, Job holds nothing back before God.
openingText: “But now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I considered unworthy to put with my sheep dogs.

title: Job 31: Final Oath of Clean Hands & Open Doors
subtitle: Summing up his entire life—generous to servants, travelers, and neighbors—Job rests his case.
summaryHook: Summing up his entire life—generous to servants, travelers, and neighbors—Job rests his case.
bigPictureText: Standing upright in solemn integrity before the throne of heaven, Job signs his defense and waits silently for God’s answer.
openingText: “I made a covenant with my eyes, how then should I look lustfully at a young woman?

title: Job 32: Young Elihu Speaks After Waiting
subtitle: Having kept quiet out of respect for gray hair, young Elihu bursts out with fresh earnestness.
summaryHook: Having kept quiet out of respect for gray hair, young Elihu bursts out with fresh earnestness.
bigPictureText: Stepping beside the silent three elders, Elihu insists wisdom belongs not merely to age but to the breath of the Almighty.
openingText: So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

title: Job 33: God Speaks Through Dreams & Rescue
subtitle: Elihu reminds Job that God is greater than mortals and often warns gently through quiet dreams and mercy.
summaryHook: Elihu reminds Job that God is greater than mortals and often warns gently through quiet dreams and mercy.
bigPictureText: Far warmer than the older friends, Elihu testifies to a God who longs to ransom weary souls back into light.
openingText: “However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.

title: Job 34: God Never Twists True Justice
subtitle: Challenging Job’s bitter complaints, Elihu defends the impartial Creator who watches every step.
summaryHook: Challenging Job’s bitter complaints, Elihu defends the impartial Creator who watches every step.
bigPictureText: Calling Job back from suggesting God ignores justice, Elihu points upward to the One who holds every breath in mercy.
openingText: Moreover Elihu answered,

title: Job 35: Look Up at High Clouds & Night Songs
subtitle: Elihu urges Job to look above clouds toward the Maker who gives songs in the night.
summaryHook: Elihu urges Job to look above clouds toward the Maker who gives songs in the night.
bigPictureText: Human sin cannot diminish the stars, nor does righteousness bargain with God—wait humbly for Him.
openingText: Moreover Elihu answered,

title: Job 36: Raindrops Drawn Up into Mist
subtitle: Elihu marvels at how God lifts water droplets gently upward into silver storm clouds to feed the earth.
summaryHook: Elihu marvels at how God lifts water droplets gently upward into silver storm clouds to feed the earth.
bigPictureText: Blending awe at thunder clouds with tender warning against bitterness, Elihu prepares the horizon for the approaching storm.
openingText: Elihu also continued, and said,

title: Job 37: Snowfall, Frost & Golden North Splendor
subtitle: Dark thunderheads gather overhead while Elihu falls silent before the breathtaking majesty of snow and lightning.
summaryHook: Dark thunderheads gather overhead while Elihu falls silent before the breathtaking majesty of snow and lightning.
bigPictureText: “Listen to this, Job! Stand still, and consider the wondrous works of God”—just before golden light breaks north through the clouds.
openingText: “Yes, at this my heart trembles, and is moved out of its place.

title: Job 38: Yahweh Speaks Out of the Whirlwind
subtitle: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth, when the morning stars sang together?”
summaryHook: “Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth, when the morning stars sang together?”
bigPictureText: Never explaining private reasons, God lovingly sweeps Job across dawn’s horizon, storehouses of snow, sea boundaries, and singing constellations.
openingText: Then Yahweh answered Job out of the whirlwind,

title: Job 39: Wild Mountain Goats, Warhorse & Eagle
subtitle: From hidden canyon deer to the fearless soaring hawk, God rejoices in untamed wild creation.
summaryHook: From hidden canyon deer to the fearless soaring hawk, God rejoices in untamed wild creation.
bigPictureText: Opening Job’s eyes beyond human utility, God celebrates wild creatures living freely under His joyful care every day.
openingText: “Do you know the time when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the doe bears fawns?

title: Job 40: Hand Over Mouth & Mighty Behemoth
subtitle: Humbled beside the Creator, Job falls quiet as God points toward riverside Behemoth among lotus reeds.
summaryHook: Humbled beside the Creator, Job falls quiet as God points toward riverside Behemoth among lotus reeds.
bigPictureText: Asking gently if a mortal can tame cosmic strength, God leads Job beside willow trees and Jordan-fed marshes in peaceful awe.
openingText: Moreover Yahweh answered Job,

title: Job 41: Fearsome Leviathan of the Foaming Deep
subtitle: “Who can strip off his outer garment?” Glimpsing untamable Leviathan blazing across dark waters.
summaryHook: “Who can strip off his outer garment?” Glimpsing untamable Leviathan blazing across dark waters.
bigPictureText: Standing before creation’s fiercest sea wonder, human pride melts away—leaving safe shelter in the only One sovereign over chaos.
openingText: “Can you draw out Leviathan with a fish hook, or press down his tongue with a cord?

title: Job 42: Seeing God & Double Restoration
subtitle: “My eyes see you!” Praying warmly for his humbled friends, Job receives twice as much and daughters fair across all the land.
summaryHook: “My eyes see you!” Praying warmly for his humbled friends, Job receives twice as much and daughters fair across all the land.
bigPictureText: True healing blooms as Job intercedes for his critics—welcoming back joyful feasts, silver, sheep, and naming three daughters of peace and beauty.
openingText: Then Job answered Yahweh,

title: Psalm 1: Tree Planted by Streams of Water
subtitle: Blessed are those who delight in God’s teaching day and night—rooted deeply beside living streams.
summaryHook: Blessed are those who delight in God’s teaching day and night—rooted deeply beside living streams.
bigPictureText: Opens the entire Psalter by contrasting hurried paths with unhurried meditation in Scripture: quiet roots that stay evergreen in every season.
openingText: Blessed is the man who doesn’t walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand on the path of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

title: Psalm 2: The Nations & God’s Anointed King
subtitle: While earthly powers scheme loudly, Heaven installs its promised King upon holy Zion.
summaryHook: While earthly powers scheme loudly, Heaven installs its promised King upon holy Zion.
bigPictureText: Voices one of Scripture’s brightest messianic anthems, calling rulers everywhere to humility and joyful refuge in the Son.
openingText: Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot a vain thing?

title: Psalm 3: Morning Peace When Surrounded
subtitle: “You, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.”
summaryHook: “You, Yahweh, are a shield around me, my glory, and the one who lifts up my head.”
bigPictureText: David’s dawn song while fleeing Absalom shows how fearless sleep grows from trusting God’s guarding presence.
openingText: Yahweh, how my adversaries have increased! Many are those who rise up against me.

title: Psalm 4: Evening Rest in Quiet Gladness
subtitle: “In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.”
summaryHook: “In peace I will both lay myself down and sleep, for you, Yahweh alone, make me live in safety.”
bigPictureText: Puts greater joy inside the heart than full barns of grain and new wine—anchoring quiet evening prayers.
openingText: Answer me when I call, God of my righteousness. Give me relief from my distress. Have mercy on me, and hear my prayer.

title: Psalm 5: Morning Prayer Beside the Sanctuary
subtitle: “In the morning, Yahweh, you will hear my voice; I will lay my requests before you and wait expectantly.”
summaryHook: “In the morning, Yahweh, you will hear my voice; I will lay my requests before you and wait expectantly.”
bigPictureText: Models dawn attentiveness—bringing honest grief alongside unwavering confidence in God’s steadfast love.
openingText: Give ear to my words, Yahweh. Consider my meditation.

title: Psalm 6: Tears Softened by Hearing Grace
subtitle: “Yahweh has heard the voice of my weeping; Yahweh accepts my prayer.”
summaryHook: “Yahweh has heard the voice of my weeping; Yahweh accepts my prayer.”
bigPictureText: Raw agony shifts suddenly into bright certainty that God never turns deaf ears toward tear-stained prayers.
openingText: Yahweh, don’t rebuke me in your anger, neither discipline me in your wrath.

title: Psalm 7: Taking Refuge in the Righteous Judge
subtitle: Slandered unfairly, David trusts the God who searches hearts and defends the upright.
summaryHook: Slandered unfairly, David trusts the God who searches hearts and defends the upright.
bigPictureText: Commits false accusations to the impartial Judge of all peoples rather than seeking bitter revenge.
openingText: Yahweh, my God, I take refuge in you. Save me from all those who pursue me, and deliver me,

title: Psalm 8: Stars Overhead & Human Dignity
subtitle: “When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers... what is man that you remember him?”
summaryHook: “When I consider your heavens, the work of your fingers... what is man that you remember him?”
bigPictureText: Standing beneath vast midnight stars, David marvels that the Creator crowns ordinary mortals with royal care over earth.
openingText: Yahweh, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens!

title: Psalm 9: Wholehearted Thanks for Justice
subtitle: “Yahweh will also be a high tower for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.”
summaryHook: “Yahweh will also be a high tower for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.”
bigPictureText: Declares those who know God’s faithful name are never abandoned when seeking Him in honest humility.
openingText: I will give thanks to Yahweh with my whole heart. I will tell of all your marvelous works.

title: Psalm 10: Rising Up for the Fatherless & Meek
subtitle: From “Why stand far off?” to confident praise that Yahweh hears every cry of the helpless.
summaryHook: From “Why stand far off?” to confident praise that Yahweh hears every cry of the helpless.
bigPictureText: Proves bold questioning of injustice leads straight to trusting God’s defending hand over the vulnerable.
openingText: Why do you stand far off, Yahweh? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?

title: Psalm 11: Standing Firm When Foundations Shake
subtitle: Even if timid voices urge fleeing like a panicked bird, Yahweh watches faithfully from His throne.
summaryHook: Even if timid voices urge fleeing like a panicked bird, Yahweh watches faithfully from His throne.
bigPictureText: Reminds anxious hearts that shaking headlines never rattle God’s steady sovereignty above.
openingText: In Yahweh, I take refuge. How can you say to my soul, “Flee as a bird to your mountain”?

title: Psalm 12: Pure Words Refined Seven Times
subtitle: In a noisy world of flattery and boastful tongues, Yahweh’s promises shine pure like silver.
summaryHook: In a noisy world of flattery and boastful tongues, Yahweh’s promises shine pure like silver.
bigPictureText: Guards the weary spirit with trustworthy Scripture stronger than human spin.
openingText: Help, Yahweh; for the godly man ceases. For the faithful fail from among the children of men.

title: Psalm 13: From “How Long?” to Singing Hope
subtitle: Four urgent “How long?” cries melt cleanly into trust in God’s unfailing mercy.
summaryHook: Four urgent “How long?” cries melt cleanly into trust in God’s unfailing mercy.
bigPictureText: A classic six-verse pattern teaching believers how honest lament moves naturally toward steady worship.
openingText: How long, Yahweh? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?

title: Psalm 14: Longing for Zion’s Salvation
subtitle: Observing widespread foolishness, the psalmist aches for God to restore captive joy in Israel.
summaryHook: Observing widespread foolishness, the psalmist aches for God to restore captive joy in Israel.
bigPictureText: Refrains from cynicism by staying anchored inside the congregation where God dwells.
openingText: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt. They have done abominable deeds. There is no one who does good.

title: Psalm 15: Who May Dwell on God’s Holy Hill?
subtitle: Walking in blameless honesty, speaking truth from the heart, and keeping promises even when it costs.
summaryHook: Walking in blameless honesty, speaking truth from the heart, and keeping promises even when it costs.
bigPictureText: Celebrates quiet integrity with neighbors and clean finances as true sanctuary worship.
openingText: Yahweh, who shall dwell in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your holy hill?

title: Psalm 16: Fullness of Joy & Safe Inheritance
subtitle: “In your presence is fullness of joy; in your right hand there are pleasures forevermore.”
summaryHook: “In your presence is fullness of joy; in your right hand there are pleasures forevermore.”
bigPictureText: David’s joyful song of shelter becomes an eternal promise of life beyond the grave.
openingText: Preserve me, God, for I take refuge in you.

title: Psalm 17: Guarded Under the Shadow of Wings
subtitle: “Keep me as the apple of your eye; hide me under the shadow of your wings.”
summaryHook: “Keep me as the apple of your eye; hide me under the shadow of your wings.”
bigPictureText: Prays earnestly through midnight testing, longing simply to wake satisfied with seeing God’s face.
openingText: Hear, Yahweh, my righteous plea; Give ear to my prayer, that doesn’t go out of deceitful lips.

title: Psalm 18: Rock, Fortress & Rescue from Deep Waters
subtitle: David’s grand victory hymn after decades of rescue from Saul and surrounding armies.
summaryHook: David’s grand victory hymn after decades of rescue from Saul and surrounding armies.
bigPictureText: Pictures Heaven bending low through storm clouds to pull a drowning servant up onto spacious solid ground.
openingText: I love you, Yahweh, my strength.

title: Psalm 19: Silent Skies & Sweet Scripture
subtitle: “The heavens declare the glory of God!”—matched inside by laws sweeter than dripping honeycomb.
summaryHook: “The heavens declare the glory of God!”—matched inside by laws sweeter than dripping honeycomb.
bigPictureText: Pairs creation’s silent wordless symphony across the sky with Scripture’s reviving wisdom for daily living.
openingText: The heavens declare the glory of God. The expanse shows his handiwork.

title: Psalm 20: Trusting God’s Name Over Chariots
subtitle: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of Yahweh our God.”
summaryHook: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of Yahweh our God.”
bigPictureText: An assembly blessing prayed over a king heading out into danger—resting strength in sanctuary help rather than weapons.
openingText: May Yahweh answer you in the day of trouble. May the name of the God of Jacob set you up on high,

title: Psalm 21: Crown of Pure Gold & Gladness
subtitle: Returning from battle, king and people celebrate life prolonged and unshakable joy in Yahweh’s presence.
summaryHook: Returning from battle, king and people celebrate life prolonged and unshakable joy in Yahweh’s presence.
bigPictureText: Completes Psalm 20’s prayer by rejoicing that mercy outlasts earthly threats.
openingText: The king rejoices in your strength, Yahweh! How greatly he rejoices in your salvation!

title: Psalm 22: Suffering Cry & Praise Across All Nations
subtitle: Moving from “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” to nations bowing in grateful feast.
summaryHook: Moving from “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” to nations bowing in grateful feast.
bigPictureText: One of Israel’s deepest messianic laments—echoed word-for-word by Jesus at Calvary before triumphant universal praise.
openingText: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?

title: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd
subtitle: Green pastures, quiet waters, dark valleys comforted by rod and staff, and mercy following forever.
summaryHook: Green pastures, quiet waters, dark valleys comforted by rod and staff, and mercy following forever.
bigPictureText: Beloved by every generation, singing fearlessly that Israel’s Shepherd walks right through darkness beside His sheep.
openingText: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.

title: Psalm 24: Lift Up Your Heads, O Ancient Gates!
subtitle: “The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness”—and the King of Glory enters Jerusalem with clean hands and pure hearts.
summaryHook: “The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness”—and the King of Glory enters Jerusalem with clean hands and pure hearts.
bigPictureText: A joyful processional anthem celebrating the Creator’s sovereignty over world and sanctuary alike.
openingText: The earth is Yahweh’s, with its fullness; the world, and those who dwell in it.

title: Psalm 25: Guide Me in Your Truth & Mercy
subtitle: “Show me your ways, Yahweh; teach me your paths... remember your tender mercies from ages past.”
summaryHook: “Show me your ways, Yahweh; teach me your paths... remember your tender mercies from ages past.”
bigPictureText: An acrostic prayer trusting God to instruct humble learners patiently along winding roads.
openingText: To you, Yahweh, I lift up my soul.

title: Psalm 26: Walking Cleanly Around Your Altar
subtitle: Choosing integrity and loving the house where God’s glory dwells.
summaryHook: Choosing integrity and loving the house where God’s glory dwells.
bigPictureText: Requests honest heart-searching so footsteps stay steady on level ground.
openingText: Judge me, Yahweh, for I have walked in my integrity. I have trusted also in Yahweh without wavering.

title: Psalm 27: One Thing Have I Asked of Yahweh
subtitle: “Wait for Yahweh! Be strong, and let your heart take courage!”
summaryHook: “Wait for Yahweh! Be strong, and let your heart take courage!”
bigPictureText: Fearless radiance replaces dread of armies when one desire anchors the soul: gazing upon God’s beauty.
openingText: Yahweh is my light and my salvation. Whom shall I fear? Yahweh is the strength of my life. Of whom shall I be afraid?

title: Psalm 28: Heard Beside the Rock of Refuge
subtitle: Urgent pleading flips swiftly into overflowing praise: “Yahweh is my strength and my shield.”
summaryHook: Urgent pleading flips swiftly into overflowing praise: “Yahweh is my strength and my shield.”
bigPictureText: Demonstrates lifting empty hands upward in faith even before external troubles clear.
openingText: To you, Yahweh, I call. My rock, don’t be deaf to me, lest, if you are silent to me, I would become like those who go down into the pit.

title: Psalm 29: Voice of Yahweh Over Mighty Waters
subtitle: Seven thunderous echoes shake cedars of Lebanon before ending with quiet peace over His people.
summaryHook: Seven thunderous echoes shake cedars of Lebanon before ending with quiet peace over His people.
bigPictureText: Turns a booming Mediterranean thunderhead into a blessing of calm strength and peace.
openingText: Ascribe to Yahweh, you sons of the mighty, ascribe to Yahweh glory and strength.

title: Psalm 30: Weeping for a Night, Joy in the Morning
subtitle: “You have turned my mourning into dancing; you clothed me with gladness!”
summaryHook: “You have turned my mourning into dancing; you clothed me with gladness!”
bigPictureText: A thanksgiving song after severe illness celebrating how brief grief melts into bright dawn mercy.
openingText: I will extol you, Yahweh, for you have raised me up, and have not made my foes to rejoice over me.

title: Psalm 31: Into Your Hand I Commit My Spirit
subtitle: “My times are in your hand”—sheltered inside the secret place of God’s presence.
summaryHook: “My times are in your hand”—sheltered inside the secret place of God’s presence.
bigPictureText: Carries both whispered trust in deepest distress and bright praise for abundant goodness laid up for the humble.
openingText: In you, Yahweh, I take refuge. Let me never be disappointed. Deliver me in your righteousness.

title: Psalm 32: Joy of Honest Forgiveness
subtitle: “Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven... You are my hiding place!”
summaryHook: “Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven... You are my hiding place!”
bigPictureText: Contrasts heavy silent guilt with light, open confession—receiving surrounding songs of deliverance.
openingText: Blessed is he whose disobedience is forgiven, whose sin is covered.

title: Psalm 33: Singing New Praise to the Creator
subtitle: “By Yahweh’s word were the heavens made”—His watchful eye rests on all who hope in His loving kindness.
summaryHook: “By Yahweh’s word were the heavens made”—His watchful eye rests on all who hope in His loving kindness.
bigPictureText: A vibrant ten-string harp hymn reminding nations that God’s loving plans outlast human strategies.
openingText: Rejoice in Yahweh, you righteous! Praise is fitting for the upright.

title: Psalm 34: Taste & See That Yahweh Is Good
subtitle: “This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.”
summaryHook: “This poor man cried, and Yahweh heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.”
bigPictureText: Sung after escaping perilous exile at Gath—inviting brokenhearted sufferers right into sheltering grace.
openingText: I will bless Yahweh at all times. His praise will always be in my mouth.

title: Psalm 35: Rescue for the Falsely Accused
subtitle: Pleading for God’s shield against unkind witnesses who return evil for good.
summaryHook: Pleading for God’s shield against unkind witnesses who return evil for good.
bigPictureText: Surrenders vengeance to God while committing every day to quiet gratitude.
openingText: Contend, Yahweh, with those who contend with me. Fight against those who fight against me.

title: Psalm 36: Loving Kindness Reaching to the Skies
subtitle: “With you is the fountain of life; in your light we will see light.”
summaryHook: “With you is the fountain of life; in your light we will see light.”
bigPictureText: Contrasts dark scheming with God’s boundless faithfulness towering higher than mountain peaks.
openingText: A revelation is within my heart about the disobedience of the wicked: “There is no fear of God before his eyes.”

title: Psalm 37: Fret Not—Wait Patiently & Inherit Peace
subtitle: “Delight yourself also in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart.”
summaryHook: “Delight yourself also in Yahweh, and he will give you the desires of your heart.”
bigPictureText: Calm elderly wisdom advising hurried souls not to envy noisy cheats, because meek goodness endures.
openingText: Don’t fret because of evildoers, neither be envious against those who work unrighteousness.

title: Psalm 38: Heavy Burden Brought Openly to God
subtitle: Bowed down under sorrow and loneliness, the psalmist waits silently upon the Lord his Savior.
summaryHook: Bowed down under sorrow and loneliness, the psalmist waits silently upon the Lord his Savior.
bigPictureText: Proves believers never need cheerful masks before praying truthfully when weak.
openingText: Yahweh, don’t rebuke me in your wrath, neither chasten me in your hot displeasure.

title: Psalm 39: Measuring Our Brevity Like a Breath
subtitle: “Show me my life’s end... surely every man walks in a shadow; my hope is in you!”
summaryHook: “Show me my life’s end... surely every man walks in a shadow; my hope is in you!”
bigPictureText: Slows down restless chasing by holding fleeting days gently before eternal mercy.
openingText: I said, “I will watch my ways, so that I don’t sin with my tongue. I will keep my mouth with a bridle while the wicked is before me.”

title: Psalm 40: Lifted Out of the Miry Clay
subtitle: “I waited patiently for Yahweh... He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.”
summaryHook: “I waited patiently for Yahweh... He set my feet on a rock, and gave me a firm place to stand.”
bigPictureText: Exchanges burnt formalities for joyful obedience and a brand-new song of deliverance.
openingText: I waited patiently for Yahweh. He turned to me, and heard my cry.

title: Psalm 41: Blessing Those Who Care for the Weak
subtitle: Even betrayed by a trusted friend at table, quiet integrity finds healing strength.
summaryHook: Even betrayed by a trusted friend at table, quiet integrity finds healing strength.
bigPictureText: Opens and closes Book I of the Psalms with compassionate faithfulness toward the poor.
openingText: Blessed is he who considers the poor. Yahweh will deliver him in the day of evil.

title: Psalm 42: As the Deer Pants for Water Brooks
subtitle: “Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God, for I shall still praise him!”
summaryHook: “Why are you cast down, O my soul? Hope in God, for I shall still praise him!”
bigPictureText: Sons of Korah launch Book II in northern exile near Mount Hermon—turning homesick tears into hopeful dialogue with the soul.
openingText: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.

title: Psalm 43: Send Out Your Light & Truth
subtitle: Asking God’s shining light to lead straight back to His joyful altar with the harp.
summaryHook: Asking God’s shining light to lead straight back to His joyful altar with the harp.
bigPictureText: Concludes Psalm 42’s longing refrain with bright courage and musical anticipation.
openingText: Vindicate me, God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation. Oh, deliver me from deceitful and wicked men.

title: Psalm 44: Remembering Ancient Mercy Through Confusion
subtitle: Puzzled by faithful devotion meeting painful defeat, the community cries, “Awake, redeem us for your loving kindness!”
summaryHook: Puzzled by faithful devotion meeting painful defeat, the community cries, “Awake, redeem us for your loving kindness!”
bigPictureText: Models bold communal lament that clings to past wonders even amid unanswered seasons.
openingText: We have heard with our ears, God; our fathers have told us what work you did in their days, in the days of old.

title: Psalm 45: Royal Wedding Song of Beauty & Truth
subtitle: “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; a scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom.”
summaryHook: “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; a scepter of equity is the scepter of your kingdom.”
bigPictureText: A radiant bridal celebration uniting righteous courage, ivory palaces, and eternal royalty.
openingText: My heart overflows with a noble theme. I recite my verses for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skillful writer.

title: Psalm 46: “Be Still & Know That I Am God”
subtitle: Though mountains fall into roaring seas, a gentle river gladdens the city of God.
summaryHook: Though mountains fall into roaring seas, a gentle river gladdens the city of God.
bigPictureText: Unshakable wartime courage resting in the serene peace of Yahweh of Armies beside us.
openingText: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.

title: Psalm 47: Clap Your Hands, All You Nations!
subtitle: Celebrates God ascending amid trumpets and joyful shouts as King over every earth kingdom.
summaryHook: Celebrates God ascending amid trumpets and joyful shouts as King over every earth kingdom.
bigPictureText: Envisions scattered peoples gathered lovingly alongside Abraham’s God.
openingText: Oh clap your hands, all you nations. Shout to God with the voice of triumph!

title: Psalm 48: Joy of All the Earth on Mount Zion
subtitle: Walk around Zion’s towers and tell the next generation that this God guides us forevermore.
summaryHook: Walk around Zion’s towers and tell the next generation that this God guides us forevermore.
bigPictureText: Marvels at peaceful sanctuary protection stronger than mighty fleets.
openingText: Great is Yahweh, and greatly to be praised, in the city of our God, in his holy mountain.

title: Psalm 49: Wealth Cannot Ransom a Single Soul
subtitle: Calling both rich and poor to hear wisdom’s riddle: gold stays behind, while God redeems His loved ones.
summaryHook: Calling both rich and poor to hear wisdom’s riddle: gold stays behind, while God redeems His loved ones.
bigPictureText: Resets worldly anxieties about money beside eternity’s horizon.
openingText: Hear this, all you peoples. Listen, all you inhabitants of the world,

title: Psalm 50: The Earth Summoned Before True Worship
subtitle: Asaph reminds Israel that God owns every cattle on a thousand hills—desiring thankful hearts over empty rituals.
summaryHook: Asaph reminds Israel that God owns every cattle on a thousand hills—desiring thankful hearts over empty rituals.
bigPictureText: Calls believers away from mechanical offerings toward gratitude, kept vows, and merciful deeds.
openingText: The Mighty One, God, Yahweh, speaks, and calls the earth from sunrise to sunset.

title: Psalm 51: Create in Me a Clean Heart, O God
subtitle: “Wash me thoroughly... a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”
summaryHook: “Wash me thoroughly... a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.”
bigPictureText: David’s immortal prayer of genuine repentance after Nathan’s visit—relying purely on vast unfailing grace.
openingText: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.

title: Psalm 52: Like a Flourishing Green Olive Tree
subtitle: Boastful cruelty withers swiftly like plucked weeds, while those trusting God’s mercy thrive forever.
summaryHook: Boastful cruelty withers swiftly like plucked weeds, while those trusting God’s mercy thrive forever.
bigPictureText: Celebrates quiet faithfulness blooming steadily inside God’s courtyard.
openingText: Why do you boast of mischief, mighty man? God’s loving kindness endures continually.

title: Psalm 53: Longing for Captives’ Joyful Return
subtitle: Echoing Psalm 14’s plea, yearning for rescue streaming forth from Zion.
summaryHook: Echoing Psalm 14’s plea, yearning for rescue streaming forth from Zion.
bigPictureText: Turns sorrow over corrupt society into fervent prayer for healing redemption.
openingText: The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt, and have done abominable iniquity. There is no one who does good.

title: Psalm 54: God Is My Helper & Sustainer
subtitle: Betrayed to Saul by neighbors at Ziph, David trusts God to uphold his life quietly.
summaryHook: Betrayed to Saul by neighbors at Ziph, David trusts God to uphold his life quietly.
bigPictureText: Finds peace amid betrayal by leaning on God’s faithful upholding hand.
openingText: Save me, God, by your name. Vindicate me in your might.

title: Psalm 55: Wings Like a Dove & Cast Your Burden
subtitle: “Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you!”—spoken through the ache of a close friend’s betrayal.
summaryHook: “Cast your burden on Yahweh, and he will sustain you!”—spoken through the ache of a close friend’s betrayal.
bigPictureText: Turns longing to fly away cleanly into steady trust morning, noon, and night.
openingText: Listen to my prayer, God. Don’t hide yourself from my supplication.

title: Psalm 56: Tears Stored in Your Bottle
subtitle: “When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you”—you record every wandering step and tear.
summaryHook: “When I am afraid, I will put my trust in you”—you record every wandering step and tear.
bigPictureText: Hunted among enemies in Gath, David celebrates a tender God who remembers every silent cry.
openingText: Be merciful to me, God, for man wants to swallow me up. All day long, he attacks and oppresses me.

title: Psalm 57: Waking the Dawn with Harp & Lyre
subtitle: Hidden inside a dark mountain cave, David vows to awake dawn itself with praise.
summaryHook: Hidden inside a dark mountain cave, David vows to awake dawn itself with praise.
bigPictureText: Danger inside stone shadows turns into global worship rising higher than the skies.
openingText: Be merciful to me, God, be merciful to me, for my soul takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.

title: Psalm 58: Calling Corrupt Judges to Account
subtitle: Denouncing rigged earthly courts while reminding earth there truly is a God who judges fairly.
summaryHook: Denouncing rigged earthly courts while reminding earth there truly is a God who judges fairly.
bigPictureText: Defends moral order when powerful institutions betray weak neighbors.
openingText: Do you indeed speak righteousness, silent ones? Do you judge blamelessly, you sons of men?

title: Psalm 59: Morning Song Beside Watchmen
subtitle: “I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning, for you have been my high tower!”
summaryHook: “I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning, for you have been my high tower!”
bigPictureText: Surrounded overnight by Saul’s guards, David greets sunrise with bright strength.
openingText: Deliver me from my enemies, my God. Set me on high from those who rise up against me.

title: Psalm 60: Shaken Land & Unfailing Banner
subtitle: Praying boldly through military setback: “Give us help against the adversary, for human help is vain.”
summaryHook: Praying boldly through military setback: “Give us help against the adversary, for human help is vain.”
bigPictureText: Holds tight to God’s covenant banner even when plans fracture unexpectedly.
openingText: God, you have rejected us. You have broken us down. You have been angry. Restore us, again.

title: Psalm 61: Lead Me to the Rock Higher Than I
subtitle: Calling from the ends of the earth for shelter beneath God’s enduring wings.
summaryHook: Calling from the ends of the earth for shelter beneath God’s enduring wings.
bigPictureText: A short aching prayer finding instant refuge on high unshakable ground.
openingText: Hear my cry, God. Listen to my prayer.

title: Psalm 62: My Soul Waits in Silence for God Alone
subtitle: “He alone is my rock and my salvation... pour out your heart before him!”
summaryHook: “He alone is my rock and my salvation... pour out your heart before him!”
bigPictureText: Resists illusions of power or riches by resting silently on steadfast mercy.
openingText: My soul rests in God alone. My salvation is from him.

title: Psalm 63: Thirsting in a Dry & Weary Land
subtitle: “Because your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you!”
summaryHook: “Because your loving kindness is better than life, my lips shall praise you!”
bigPictureText: Deep Judean wilderness thirst transforms into rich midnight meditation on God’s beauty.
openingText: God, you are my God. I will earnestly seek you. My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

title: Psalm 64: Sheltered from Whispered Traps
subtitle: Secret plots fail quickly when righteous hearts take quiet gladness in Yahweh.
summaryHook: Secret plots fail quickly when righteous hearts take quiet gladness in Yahweh.
bigPictureText: Reassures anxious hearts against malicious gossip and hidden snares.
openingText: Hear my voice, God, in my complaint. Preserve my life from fear of the enemy.

title: Psalm 65: Crowning the Year with Harvest Bounty
subtitle: From silenced roaring seas to rain-softened pastures dressed in flocks and singing valleys.
summaryHook: From silenced roaring seas to rain-softened pastures dressed in flocks and singing valleys.
bigPictureText: A lush thanksgiving hymn celebrating how God’s river waters every green field.
openingText: Praise waits for you, God, in Zion. Vows shall be performed to you.

title: Psalm 66: Through Fire & Water to Rich Abundance
subtitle: “Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will declare what he has done for my soul!”
summaryHook: “Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will declare what he has done for my soul!”
bigPictureText: Invites every land to test-and-see how God brings refined pilgrims cleanly into spacious blessing.
openingText: Make a joyful shout to God, all the earth!

title: Psalm 67: May Your Face Shine Across Every Nation
subtitle: Echoing Aaron’s blessing so earth’s farthest corners know God’s saving goodness and fair joy.
summaryHook: Echoing Aaron’s blessing so earth’s farthest corners know God’s saving goodness and fair joy.
bigPictureText: Links harvest gratitude at home directly with blessing every family on earth.
openingText: May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us.

title: Psalm 68: Triumphal Procession from Sinai to Zion
subtitle: Father of the fatherless and defender of widows—riding heavens in joyful victory.
summaryHook: Father of the fatherless and defender of widows—riding heavens in joyful victory.
bigPictureText: Celebrates God leading lonely captives into warm families with tambourines and choirs.
openingText: Let God arise! Let his enemies be scattered! Let them who hate him also flee before him.

title: Psalm 69: Sinking in Deep Waters Yet Still Praising
subtitle: “Zeal for your house has eaten me up!”—answered by God’s immense mercy for weary prisoners.
summaryHook: “Zeal for your house has eaten me up!”—answered by God’s immense mercy for weary prisoners.
bigPictureText: Speaks raw agony alongside radiant certainty that God hears needy souls.
openingText: Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!

title: Psalm 70: Urgent Five-Verse Cry for Swift Help
subtitle: “Make haste to me, O God! You are my help and my deliverer—Yahweh, don’t delay.”
summaryHook: “Make haste to me, O God! You are my help and my deliverer—Yahweh, don’t delay.”
bigPictureText: Teaches that shortest breathless prayers in crisis rise powerfully to heaven.
openingText: Hurry, God, to deliver me. Come quickly to help me, Yahweh.

title: Psalm 71: Faithful Companion from Youth to Gray Hair
subtitle: “Don’t forsake me when I am old and gray, O God, until I declare your strength to the next generation.”
summaryHook: “Don’t forsake me when I am old and gray, O God, until I declare your strength to the next generation.”
bigPictureText: An elderly saint’s tender prayer turning lifelong memory into mentor-hope for children.
openingText: In you, Yahweh, I take refuge. Never let me be disappointed.

title: Psalm 72: Gentle Rain Upon Mown Grass (Solomon’s King)
subtitle: Prays for a righteous ruler defending poor children like gentle showers watering fresh earth.
summaryHook: Prays for a righteous ruler defending poor children like gentle showers watering fresh earth.
bigPictureText: Closes Book II with soaring messianic vision: peace blooming till the moon is no more.
openingText: God, give the king your justice; your righteousness to the royal son.

title: Psalm 73: Footsteps Steadied Inside the Sanctuary
subtitle: Asaph nearly slipped envying arrogant wealth—until stepping inside worship shifted everything cleanly: “Whom have I in heaven but you?”
summaryHook: Asaph nearly slipped envying arrogant wealth—until stepping inside worship shifted everything cleanly: “Whom have I in heaven but you?”
bigPictureText: Opens Book III with honest struggle over unfairness healed by drawing near to God.
openingText: Surely God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.

title: Psalm 74: Grieving Burned Sanctuary Yet Remembering Creation
subtitle: Standing amid ruined sanctuary stones, Asaph recalls how God split ancient seas and framed summer and winter.
summaryHook: Standing amid ruined sanctuary stones, Asaph recalls how God split ancient seas and framed summer and winter.
bigPictureText: Brings shattered national grief boldly before covenant promises.
openingText: God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?

title: Psalm 75: God Alone Lifts Up & Humbles
subtitle: Remind proud horns not to boast loudly—for promotion belongs to earth’s fair Judge.
summaryHook: Remind proud horns not to boast loudly—for promotion belongs to earth’s fair Judge.
bigPictureText: Thanks God in advance that His nearness always sets crooked scales upright.
openingText: We give thanks to you, God. We give thanks, for your Name is near. Men tell about your wondrous works.

title: Psalm 76: Awesome Stillness When God Rises
subtitle: Brighter than mountain prey, God rescues the humble of earth calmly without noisy bluster.
summaryHook: Brighter than mountain prey, God rescues the humble of earth calmly without noisy bluster.
bigPictureText: Celebrates Judah’s quiet shelter under God’s tabernacle at Salem.
openingText: In Judah, God is known. His name is great in Israel.

title: Psalm 77: Remembering Red Sea Paths in Sleepless Night
subtitle: Unable to sleep from deep distress, Asaph traces God’s footsteps hidden through mighty waters.
summaryHook: Unable to sleep from deep distress, Asaph traces God’s footsteps hidden through mighty waters.
bigPictureText: Heals dark midnight anxiety by remembering ancient saving faithfulness.
openingText: My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help, and for him to listen to me.

title: Psalm 78: Storytelling Faith to Coming Generations
subtitle: Asaph’s sweeping epic retelling Exodus wonders and wandering rebellion so children don’t forget God.
summaryHook: Asaph’s sweeping epic retelling Exodus wonders and wandering rebellion so children don’t forget God.
bigPictureText: Passes living history down so the next generation sets hope squarely in God—ending with shepherd David.
openingText: Hear my teaching, my people. Turn your ears to the words of my mouth.

title: Psalm 79: How Long? Mercy Over Ruined Jerusalem
subtitle: Grieving fallen temple courts, the community pleads purely for compassionate pardon.
summaryHook: Grieving fallen temple courts, the community pleads purely for compassionate pardon.
bigPictureText: Relies not on past merit but entirely on God’s rescuing reputation and shepherd care.
openingText: God, the nations have come into your inheritance. They have defiled your holy temple. They have laid Jerusalem in heaps.

title: Psalm 80: Restore Us, Shepherd of Israel
subtitle: “Turn us again, O God; cause your face to shine, and we shall be saved!”
summaryHook: “Turn us again, O God; cause your face to shine, and we shall be saved!”
bigPictureText: Likens Israel to an uprooted Egypt-vine needing God’s tender sunlight again.
openingText: Hear us, Shepherd of Israel, you who lead Joseph like a flock, you who sit above the cherubim, shine out.

title: Psalm 81: Trumpet Feast & “Open Your Mouth Wide”
subtitle: “Oh, that my people would listen to me—I would feed them with finest wheat and honey from the rock!”
summaryHook: “Oh, that my people would listen to me—I would feed them with finest wheat and honey from the rock!”
bigPictureText: Links joyful tambourine celebration with tender invitation to joyful obedience.
openingText: Sing aloud to God, our strength! Make a joyful shout to the God of Jacob!

title: Psalm 82: Defend the Weak & Orphan
subtitle: Heavenly courtroom summons urging earthly rulers to rescue the destitute from wicked grip.
summaryHook: Heavenly courtroom summons urging earthly rulers to rescue the destitute from wicked grip.
bigPictureText: Proclaims justice for vulnerable neighbors as the heartbeat of divine rule.
openingText: God presides in the great assembly. He judges among the gods.

title: Psalm 83: Surrounded Yet Trusting God’s Name
subtitle: Facing hostile coalitions, Asaph prays enemies recognize Yahweh alone rules over all the earth.
summaryHook: Facing hostile coalitions, Asaph prays enemies recognize Yahweh alone rules over all the earth.
bigPictureText: Even prayers for rescue aim ultimately toward nations discovering the true Lord.
openingText: God, don’t keep silent. Don’t keep silent, and don’t be still, God.

title: Psalm 84: Better Is One Day in Your Courts
subtitle: “Even the sparrow has found a home... blessed are those whose strength is in you!”
summaryHook: “Even the sparrow has found a home... blessed are those whose strength is in you!”
bigPictureText: Pilgrims turning dry weeping valleys into refreshing spring pools on the walk toward Zion.
openingText: How lovely are your dwellings, Yahweh of Armies!

title: Psalm 85: Mercy & Truth Meet Together
subtitle: “Righteousness and peace have kissed each other!”—reviving dry soil into blooming harvest.
summaryHook: “Righteousness and peace have kissed each other!”—reviving dry soil into blooming harvest.
bigPictureText: Radiant prophecy of spiritual renewal uniting honest truth with tender peace.
openingText: Yahweh, you have been favorable to your land. You have restored the fortunes of Jacob.

title: Psalm 86: Teach Me Your Way & Unite My Heart
subtitle: “Unite my heart to fear your name... You, Lord, are slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness.”
summaryHook: “Unite my heart to fear your name... You, Lord, are slow to anger and abundant in loving kindness.”
bigPictureText: David echoes Moses at Sinai (Exodus 34:6) for undivided quiet courage.
openingText: Hear, Yahweh, and answer me, for I am poor and needy.

title: Psalm 87: All Nations Born Inside Zion
subtitle: Astonishingly lists former enemies—Egypt, Babylon, Tyre—written proudly as citizens of Zion.
summaryHook: Astonishingly lists former enemies—Egypt, Babylon, Tyre—written proudly as citizens of Zion.
bigPictureText: Previews global gospel welcome where every culture finds home in God’s city.
openingText: His foundation is in the holy mountains.

title: Psalm 88: Prayer Without Easy Resolution in Darkness
subtitle: Closing purely in shadows and loneliness, Heman proves faithful prayer still speaks to the God of salvation.
summaryHook: Closing purely in shadows and loneliness, Heman proves faithful prayer still speaks to the God of salvation.
bigPictureText: Gives courageous permission to keep praying honestly even before dawn breaks.
openingText: Yahweh, the God of my salvation, I have cried day and night before you.

title: Psalm 89: Unfailing Covenant & Piercing Lament
subtitle: Opens praising God’s eternal promise to David before grieving painfully how shattered the throne looks.
summaryHook: Opens praising God’s eternal promise to David before grieving painfully how shattered the throne looks.
bigPictureText: Closes Book III wrestling honestly with promise versus crisis—ending in faithful blessing anyway.
openingText: I will sing of the loving kindness of Yahweh forever. With my mouth, I will make known your faithfulness to all generations.

title: Psalm 90: Our Dwelling Place for All Generations (Moses)
subtitle: “Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom!”
summaryHook: “Teach us to number our days, that we may gain a heart of wisdom!”
bigPictureText: Attributed to Moses, launching Book IV by contrasting fleeting grass with eternal mountain-maker love.
openingText: Lord, you have been our dwelling place for all generations.

title: Psalm 91: Resting Under the Shadow of the Almighty
subtitle: “He will cover you with his feathers; under his wings you will take refuge.”
summaryHook: “He will cover you with his feathers; under his wings you will take refuge.”
bigPictureText: Peaceful assurance wrapped gently around nights of fear, pestilence, and steep mountain trails.
openingText: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

title: Psalm 92: Flourishing Like Cedars in Lebanon (Sabbath)
subtitle: “It is good to give thanks to Yahweh... still bringing forth fresh green fruit in old age!”
summaryHook: “It is good to give thanks to Yahweh... still bringing forth fresh green fruit in old age!”
bigPictureText: A joyful Sabbath celebration watching faithful lives deepen gracefully over decades.
openingText: It is a good thing to give thanks to Yahweh, to sing praises to your name, Most High,

title: Psalm 93: Yahweh Reigns Above Roaring Floods
subtitle: Clothed in majesty above crashing ocean breakers, God’s throne stands unmoved from ancient days.
summaryHook: Clothed in majesty above crashing ocean breakers, God’s throne stands unmoved from ancient days.
bigPictureText: Begins the “Yahweh Reigns!” royal anthem series anchoring chaos under eternal beauty.
openingText: Yahweh reigns! He is clothed with majesty! Yahweh is armed with strength. The world also is established. It can’t be moved.

title: Psalm 94: Teacher of Mankind & Quiet Consolation
subtitle: “When my thoughts were many within me, your comforts cheered my soul!”
summaryHook: “When my thoughts were many within me, your comforts cheered my soul!”
bigPictureText: Reassures weary hearts that the Maker of eyes and ears never overlooks quiet tears.
openingText: Yahweh, you God to whom vengeance belongs, you God to whom vengeance belongs, shine out.

title: Psalm 95: Come Let Us Bow Down & Listen Today
subtitle: “Shout aloud to the rock of our salvation!”—followed gently by “Today, if you hear his voice, don’t harden your heart.”
